currentContext.business: The business of the Company is manufacturing and marketing of auto components for the transportation industry, viz., steering and suspension linkage products, steering gear products, aluminium alloy based high pressure die-casting products, brake components and engine components. It serves Indian and overseas OEMs across passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, farm tractors and two-wheelers, and also sells into the automotive aftermarket through a distribution network. Following the Scheme of Amalgamation with erstwhile Rane Engine Valve Limited and erstwhile Rane Brake Lining Limited, the Company now reports as an amalgamated entity spanning five businesses: Steering & Linkages, Light Metal Castings, Engine Components, Brake Components and Aftermarket Products.

Light Metal Castings: Aluminium alloy based high pressure die-casting products
Aftermarket Products: Aftermarket auto components across the company product lines

currentContext.expansion: The routed bundle carries no named capex project, capacity addition, commissioning or ramp-up plan. The only footprint disclosure is in Corporate Information, which states Plant Locations of 15 in India and 1 outside India (through subsidiary). The overseas footprint sits in two subsidiaries - Rane (Madras) International Holdings B.V., The Netherlands, which holds the Company's foreign strategic investments, and Rane Automotive Components Mexico S de R.L. de C.V., which is in the business of steering and linkage auto components; total investments as on March 31, 2026 by the Company in RACM and RMIH are MXN$ 19.03 million and Euro 4.32 million respectively. On funding stance, the MD&A risk table states that borrowings are used to fund expansion and that the Company manages interest rate risk by maintaining optimal debt-equity levels and by doing 'Capex primarily through internal accruals', constantly optimising working capital to reduce interest costs. Capacity-adjacent operational initiatives mentioned are the Quality DOJO rollout across plants and the RMSP 4.0 framework, under which 102 Productivity, Quality, Cost, Delivery and Safety improvement projects were completed during the year. The Company's scale expanded through the Scheme of Amalgamation with erstwhile Rane Engine Valve Limited and erstwhile Rane Brake Lining Limited (shares allotted April 23, 2025) rather than through a disclosed greenfield project.

risks.risk: Industry / market concentration on the Indian automotive sector
risks.note: A major portion of revenue is derived from the Indian automotive sector, so any drop in vehicle production will have a significant impact on the Company's business. Management is responding by increasing revenue from international markets, adding new products to grow organic revenue and diversifying customers across vehicle businesses.

risks.risk: Price-down pressure on newly secured products
risks.note: Management flags in the same risk row that new products secured by the Company are at significantly lower sale prices and pose a significant risk in terms of profitability; the Company is pursuing dialogue with customers for price increases against the global environment and increasing cost pressures.

risks.risk: Technology obsolescence in the auto component portfolio
risks.note: Changes in the auto industry and customer preference can render technology obsolete. Mitigants cited are enhanced R&D capabilities, localisation of testing and validation, and a portfolio spread across steering, engine, braking and transmission components serving vehicle businesses at different levels of technology adoption.

Maintaining market share in competitive markets and the availability of unorganised players pose a challenge; the Company relies on long-standing OEM relationships, its facilities and processes, and periodic customer surveys.

Material cost is a significant part of total cost and volatility in raw material prices will erode margin. Mitigation is via cost reduction through alternate sourcing and localisation, negotiating pass-through of input cost increases to customers, and process and yield improvements.

risks.risk: Foreign currency exposure on exports and imported raw materials
risks.note: The Company exports products to various countries and imports raw materials, exposing it to exchange-rate risk. It balances imports and exports for a natural hedge, works with customers to index prices, and takes forwards on a rolling basis to protect export realisation.

risks.risk: Interest rate risk on borrowings used to fund expansion
risks.note: Use of borrowings to fund expansion exposes the Company to interest rate risk; it manages this by maintaining optimal debt-equity levels, funding capex primarily through internal accruals, optimising working capital and leveraging banking relationships. The FY26 debt-equity ratio improved to 0.82 standalone from 1.10, aided by debt reduction from advance land sale proceeds.

risks.risk: Quality and delivery risk on safety-critical components, and attrition of key personnel
risks.note: Quality and delivery are described as sacrosanct for the safety-critical products supplied by the Group, with Quality DOJO being rolled out across plants to lift workforce skills; separately, attrition of key personnel could impact business operations and growth, addressed through HR processes, a dedicated training centre and leadership pipeline development.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.
